posts.title: Davis Cup’s current format a winning formula, says World Tennis CEO
posts.description: World Tennis CEO Ross Hutchins said the revamped Davis Cup format was a “winning formula” with its combination of home-and-away qualifying ties and a one-city Final 8. Introduced in 2025, the format restored home-and-away ties for the second qualifying round while retaining a condensed eight-team knockout stage at the end of the season. The Finals are being staged in Bologna and will remain in Italy through 2027, with Hutchins saying the event had benefited from having a settled home. “When we have a home like this, it is very compelling to stay here for as many years as possible, and we believe that we have a very good product here,” Hutchins told reporters. “But we also have significant amounts of nations around the world who are competing in this competition as well. So, we need to get that balance right, but we think that what we have today is a winning formula.” Italy are chasing a fourth consecutive title and face the Czech Republic in the semi-finals, while Spain take on Britain

posts.title: Alcaraz and Jodar fire Spain into Davis Cup final
posts.description: Carlos Alcaraz made a triumphant return to Davis Cup action on Saturday by thrashing Britain’s Arthur Fery to send Spain into a mouth-watering final showdown against holders Italy. The world number three was in total control inside the BolognaFiere Arena to outclass Fery 6-2 6-1 and give his side an unassailable 2-0 lead. Earlier, Spain’s new rising force Rafael Jodar beat a battling Cameron Norrie 6-2 7-5. Spain will now seek to avenge last year’s final loss to Italy in Sunday’s showpiece. Alcaraz had tape on his right knee and a strapping on his left thigh but was never really extended by an overpowered Fery who rose to become British number one after a stunning run to the Wimbledon semi-finals in July. The seven-times Grand Slam champion will now set his sights on ticking off one of the few major prizes to elude him by propelling Spain to their first title since 2019. Britain’s defeat ended the 16-year reign of captain Leon Smith who will now step down.

posts.title: Student-led protest against government turns violent in Albania
posts.description: Violence broke out in Albania on Saturday during a student-led protest calling for the resignation of Prime Minister Edi Rama after months of anti-government demonstrations. Demonstrators had gathered in the capital Tirana on Independence Day and threw stones and petrol bombs at riot police, who responded with water cannon, tear gas and rubber bullets. Fuelled by anger over perceived government corruption, lack of jobs and poor education standards, demonstrations have rocked Tirana since mid-October and spread to other cities. They have often turned violent, with protesters setting fire to government buildings and banks, smashing shop windows and pulling up paving stones to throw at police.
